consolidation.why_one_option: Both PRs relax THE IDENTICAL GATE -- the is_complex(orblock) decline inside rule_block_or (p8_structure/blockaction.rs) and its verbatim twin try_block_or (p8_structure/region_structurer.rs). The shared root cause is Ghidra's BlockBasic::isComplex >2-statement readability budget. They collided hard: both added a CollapseStructure field named condfold_blocks, both added a builder named with_condfold_blocks, condjoin's entry point was even named compute_condfold_blocks, and both bumped the option count 76 -> 77. They differed only in the admission predicate and the value surface.
consolidation.predicate_is_the_union: A sibling must fit the level's PRINTED-WIDTH BUDGET (<=5 comma elements at `on`, <=9 at `wide`, measured by kuna_condfold.rs printed_shape with the printer's own skip rules) and then be taken by EITHER rule. Rule A (from #193) is the bounded-prefix rule; Rule B (from #194) is the statement-shape allowlist. Neither subsumes the other -- Rule A admits a 5-to-9-statement straight-line prefix Rule B's shape/scored caps refuse, Rule B admits a second call and a NESTED BlockCondition (what a guard CASCADE needs) that Rule A never takes. Rule A is tried first at the fold site.
consolidation.condjoin_disappears: There is no `condjoin` option name, no cond_join Architecture/ArchContext field, no kuna_condjoin.rs, and no second spec section. Exactly ONE net new option: 76 -> 77.

soundness.argument: Rendering-only. BlockGraph::new_block_condition re-parents two existing structuring nodes; no p-code op is moved, reordered, cloned, or deleted. Soundness rests on a precondition rule_block_or already enforces and this option never weakens: orblock.size_in() == 1, so the sibling's statements cannot run on a path where the compound condition is not evaluated. C's short-circuit rule evaluates the right operand exactly when control used to fall into the sibling, and the comma operator is a sequence point, so the absorbed statements still run before the test, in order. The only synthesized operation is negate_condition_rec, a boolean sense flip on an already-computed condition; it is order-neutral.
soundness.proposal_56_worry_does_not_arise: Proposal #56 warned that a wrong de Morgan inversion emits wrong C because the predicates call getuid/geteuid/getegid/getgid, which cannot be reordered past one another. No such reordering is possible: the operands are never swapped, only relabelled. NO PURITY ANALYSIS IS NEEDED. Both original agents and both independent reviewers established this separately.
soundness.is_complex_blast_radius: is_complex() itself was NOT changed. The relaxation is a disjunct at the two rule_block_or/try_block_or call sites only; the other callers (rule_block_while_do and its region_structurer twin) see the unchanged verdict. This is why the 675-assertion corpus is untouched.
new_guards_all_rendering_or_quality: BOTH rules: the operand's printed comma chain is bounded by the policy level (<=5 elements at `on`, <=9 at `wide`), counted with the printer's own skip rules (not_printed / markers / implied-out / bare CPUI_BRANCH), the terminal CBRANCH included

BOTH rules: printed_shape refuses outright on a block with no terminal CPUI_CBRANCH, or with a non-terminal branch op surviving the skips (mirrors angr _build_multistatementexpr_statements refusing a non-terminal ConditionalJump or any Jump)
Rule A: orblock must be BlockType::Copy of a single BlockBasic (a BlockList/BlockIf/BlockCondition operand could render braces, multiple lines, or a label inside the parens = invalid C)

Rule B: statement-shape allowlist (marker | op with an output | void CALL/CALLIND | STORE | the single terminal CBRANCH); declines RETURN, a second branch, BRANCHIND, CALLOTHER, and any no-return call
Rule B: <=2 calc_explicit-scored statements and <=2 calls per block (counting EVERY call, unlike Rule A). The scored count is NOT a width -- see reviewer_defects_addressed
Rule B: a nested BlockCondition operand requires BOTH sub-blocks admissible (not isComplex's getBlock(0)-only delegation), plus <=4 condition leaves and <=4 total scored statements at the fold site

both rules: NO buffered comment of any type at an address the block covers (emit_basic_block_ops suppresses emit_comment_group under comma_separate, so folding would silently DELETE a WARNING: line -- decline instead)
gate: the pre-existing !orblock.is_interior_goto_target() decline is NEVER relaxed (emit_block_copy emits the label statement first, so a labelled sibling would print `label_x:` inside an expression)

gate: a relaxed fold's node is force-marked complex, because BlockCondition::isComplex delegates to sub-block 0 and would otherwise report the LEFT operand's trivial verdict for a node whose right operand is a comma chain, letting rule_block_while_do hoist the whole chain into a while(...) header

On the PR's own headline witness KUNA_CONDFOLD_DEBUG reported `admit(shape) BlockId(7v1) @ 0x40242e: 2 statement(s)` for a block that renders SEVEN statements plus the branch. Rule B's shape allowlist and call cap are UNCHANGED (they are the soundness-relevant half and are byte-identical to #194). The calc_explicit score is kept only because the cross-leaf caps MAX_JOIN_LEAVES / MAX_JOIN_TOTAL_STMTS are expressed in it.

round_2_defect_4_document_the_width_slac.fix: That sentence is gone from all four surfaces. Each now states exactly what the enforced budget bounds and what it does not.
round_2_defect_4_document_the_width_slac.what_the_budget_bounds: Per admitted leaf, the comma chain printed_shape measures is <=5 elements at `on` and <=9 at `wide`.
what_it_does_not_bound: The summed printed width of a Rule-B CASCADE's leaves: it is a per-leaf bound, and the only cross-leaf cap (MAX_JOIN_TOTAL_STMTS) is expressed in the weak calc_explicit score. Not tightened: converting that cap to printed width would decline newbury::main, whose three leaves print 2-3 elements each.

The final condition's GLOBAL width: a purely upstream-legal fold (both operands non-complex) can still extend a cascade on the LEFT without consulting any condfold cap -- exactly as it can with the option off (this disclosure is unchanged).

Post-structuring drift: the measure is taken on the op list as it stands at structuring time. On tr::build_spec_list it reads 6-9 across the structuring passes and the operand finally emits 8 elements.

It OVER-counts where a call's stack-effect ops are still live at structuring time (unprototyped callee, no frame recovery). Over-counting only ever declines a fold, so the error is in the safe direction -- but it is why the Rule-B stage witness needs `wide` while the real newbury::main closes at `on`.
kept_disclosures: the caps bound the relaxation at each site where it is EXERCISED, not the final condition's global width

speed.method: INTERLEAVED off/on/wide on CHILD CPU TIME (user+sys via os.wait4 rusage). Each iteration runs all three levels back to back so load drift cancels rather than landing in one arm; scripts.pipeline.timeit runs all-OFF-then-all-ON and is unusable under this box's variable load. Box load average during measurement: 11-14 (other users' jobs).
speed.honest_reading: THE MEASUREMENT DOES NOT RESOLVE THE OPTION'S COST ON THIS BOX, and is reported that way rather than rounded into a claim. On the small function the deltas are under 1.5%. On lighttpd main -- a 4-second outlier where the option fires several times -- two independent interleaved runs put `on` at -5.5% and +5.3%, i.e. straddling zero with a 10.8-point spread between replicates, while the OFF arm's OWN sample spread within a single run is -10% to +28% even on CPU time. `wide` is the more consistent arm at +1.4% and +1.6%. Medians are inside the 5% budget; the noise floor is larger than the effect.
speed.expected_cost: one extra predicate inside the loop that already calls bb_is_complex (skipped entirely when off), plus a set/map lookup at an existing decline, plus the two-rule precompute over the bblocks list -- which now also runs the printed_shape walk once per block per rule. The bigger term on a large function is second-order: more folds mean the fixpoint structuring loop matches more schemas, which is why `on` (fewer folds than before this fix) is not obviously slower than `off`.
speed.note: The option ships default-OFF for readability/presentation reasons, not speed. With it off the precompute is skipped and every gate disjunct is dead.

not_closed: Default-ON. That needs its own 0/675 ablation and a DIV row; the 2827-function sweep is supporting evidence (monotone improvement, no invalid C), not the ablation. The decbench regression and the comment-loss effect are both presentation arguments for staying opt-in.

The width budget is a PER-LEAF bound. A Rule-B cascade of up to 4 leaves has no bound on their summed printed width, because the only cross-leaf cap is expressed in the weak calc_explicit score. Converting that cap to printed width would decline newbury::main, so it is documented rather than tightened.

The width measure is taken at structuring time and OVER-counts where a call's stack-effect ops are still live (unprototyped callee, no frame recovery). Safe direction -- it only declines -- but it makes the option needlessly conservative on such code; the Rule-B stage witness is the reproducible case.

Rule B's cross-leaf caps are not a GLOBAL bound on the folded condition's width; a purely upstream-legal fold can extend a cascade on the left without consulting them (unchanged from the previous round).
A comment produced by a pass that runs AFTER structuring can still be dropped by the comma_separate operand (newbury::main loses one branchflip advisory).
The Rule-B stage witness no longer ISOLATES Rule B at the level it now runs at; Rule B's exclusive capability is proven by unit tests and a real-binary trace instead.
angr's four schema arms are matched only through Ghidra's ruleBlockOr shape. angr's type_b/type_d (the with-else forms) can fire on graphs ruleBlockOr's topology checks reject; those remain unfolded.
The region structurer still does not fully converge on build_spec_list; making it converge is a separate, larger opportunity.

neither_rule_subsumes_the_other.changed_by_the_review_round: The old argument -- 'the entire aggregate delta of `wide` over `on` is Rule A, because Rule B's caps do not move between levels' -- NO LONGER HOLDS: the shared width budget moves for both rules. neither_rule_subsumes_the_other.conclusion: The predicate must be the UNION. Intersecting them, or dropping either, loses a closed proposal.
